{"stage":"answer","question_id":"1B.3","answer":{"question_id":"1B.3","answer":"The evidence shows a mixed institutional record, with substantial formal nuclear-safety capacity and continuing implementation gaps, but limited proof that López Obrador personally enacted, funded, staffed, or corrected these safeguards. Mexico maintained a CNSNS-led regulatory system with inspection, enforcement, sanction, closure, and fine powers; CFE and CNSNS operated monitoring, self-assessment, peer-review, corrective-action, safety-culture, training, emergency-preparedness, spent-fuel, waste-management, and post-Fukushima programs (BATCH-0002-E002, BATCH-0002-E004, BATCH-0002-E005, BATCH-0002-E007, BATCH-0002-E008, BATCH-0002-E010, BATCH-0002-E011, BATCH-0002-E013). The IAEA also records Mexican support for safeguards, physical and nuclear safety, peer review, and technical-cooperation projects (BATCH-0031-E001, BATCH-0031-E002). These are evidence of an operating institutional framework, not by themselves proof of effective presidential stewardship or complete implementation.

Target-year evidence includes two radiological-security incidents. In March 2023, four Ir-192 devices were stolen and later recovered; inspectors verified improved security measures, with no reported exposure or injury (BATCH-0040-E011). In October 2023, organized crime stole a radiography camera containing an Ir-192 source; the IAEA recorded degraded defence in depth but no release, overexposure, contamination, injury, or continuing problem (BATCH-0038-E002). These outcomes indicate successful recovery and no reported harm, while also demonstrating custody vulnerabilities. A June 2023 biosafety committee agreement shows some formal attention to biological-risk governance, but supplies no evidence on staffing, resources, enforcement, or effectiveness (BATCH-0039-E002).

The strongest adverse evidence concerns cyber and institutional safeguards. A 2022 military data breach exposed more than four million Sedena emails; experts associated the weakness with cancelled cybersecurity equipment, insufficient personnel, and limited capacity, while López Obrador acknowledged the hack without, in the reported account, addressing the weakness or announcing a remedy (BATCH-0047-E010). Related reporting described attacks, obsolete systems, missing patches, weak risk assessment, inadequate monitoring, and unresolved vulnerabilities across federal institutions (BATCH-0011-E005). In 2023, Sedena reported thousands of cyberattack attempts and described upgrades and training, but also classified its internal investigation, filed no federal complaint, and saw an accused informatics commander provisionally released (BATCH-0008-E006). These facts support continuing command-and-control and accountability concerns, although they do not prove that López Obrador personally caused the deficiencies or directed the secrecy.

Older context shows that nuclear institutions had unresolved structural weaknesses before and into the target period: CNSNS had technical autonomy but lacked full legal-administrative independence from SENER; staffing, knowledge management, inspection, training, communication, and resources remained subjects of recommendations; no human-and-organizational-factors inspections were conducted at Laguna Verde in 2019–2021; and the plant reported equipment failures, procedural omissions, human error, access-control failures, and design or maintenance weaknesses (BATCH-0002-E002, BATCH-0002-E006, BATCH-0002-E009, BATCH-0002-E012). Post-Fukushima measures were reportedly 98% complete for actions scheduled by end-2023, but some specialized measures remained in development or pending, and waste-storage capacity was constrained (BATCH-0002-E004, BATCH-0002-E011, BATCH-0002-E013). The sources report corrective processes and regulatory review, but do not establish that every finding was closed or that the remaining gaps caused harm.

Overall, the record supports credit for maintaining and operating significant formal safeguards, regulatory powers, training, monitoring, recovery, and corrective-action systems. It also supports adverse or qualifying findings for regulator dependence, incomplete inspections and institutional reforms, recurring operational and custody failures, unresolved military cyber weaknesses, and uncertain accountability. Most nuclear evidence concerns CFE, CNSNS, SENER, and other institutions rather than direct presidential decisions; official sources are partly self-reported, and several items are inherited or pre-2023 conditions. Evidence of actual 2023 outcomes is strongest for the radiological incidents and weaker for broader effectiveness. The available record therefore supports a mixed assessment of institutional conduct and implementation, with López Obrador-specific attribution and the effectiveness of correction remaining materially uncertain.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0031-E001","BATCH-0031-E002","BATCH-0038-E002","BATCH-0039-E002","BATCH-0040-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E006","BATCH-0002-E009","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0047-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The packet provides limited direct evidence of López Obrador's personal decisions, appointments, budgets, directives, or corrective orders.","Many nuclear-safety claims come from government reports or institutional self-reporting and lack independent verification of effectiveness.","Several adverse nuclear findings concern 2019–2022 conditions or inherited institutional weaknesses rather than distinct 2023 presidential actions.","The packet does not establish final closure of all inspection findings, post-Fukushima actions, cyber vulnerabilities, or accountability proceedings.","There is no comprehensive evidence here on national continuity-of-government or strategic nuclear command-and-control beyond civilian nuclear and cyber-related institutions.","Reported absence of radiological harm does not establish that custody and accident-prevention safeguards were fully effective."]},"critique":null,"corrected":null}
